setup: Qheadache is installed and launched as a desktop application on a single computer with no other game platform or companion app open.
action: The player starts Qheadache from the computer's application launcher.
expected_observation: Qheadache opens directly as a self-contained puzzle game window and can be played without requiring another product, launcher, or companion service.

setup: A fresh Qheadache session is available with an easy introductory puzzle and a standard puzzle available from the main menu.
action: A young beginner selects the introductory puzzle, and an adult player selects a standard puzzle in separate sessions.
expected_observation: Both players can understand the on-screen puzzle board and begin play successfully, with the beginner able to engage with the easier puzzle and the adult able to use the full game interface without age-specific barriers.

setup: Qheadache is open at the main puzzle screen with a visible board containing movable blocks and an obvious goal layout.
action: The player starts a new puzzle and attempts to move blocks around the board.
expected_observation: The game displays a graphical board and allows block-moving puzzle interaction, with visible block positions changing according to the puzzle rules.

setup: Qheadache is installed on a computer that has no network connection available and no external service accounts configured.
action: The player launches the game and begins a normal puzzle session offline.
expected_observation: The puzzle loads and can be played normally without any network login, cloud dependency, or external service prompt.

setup: A product owner or sponsor is reviewing Qheadache release planning, scope boundaries, and a proposed priority change list.
action: The sponsor approves the planned scope and decides whether a requested feature should move up in priority.
expected_observation: The scope and priority change decision is finalized by the sponsor, and the approved direction is reflected in the release plan or project decision record.

setup: The development team has access to the Qheadache puzzle logic, board behavior, and tracking feature backlog.
action: A defect is found in board movement or progress tracking and is assigned to the team for correction.
expected_observation: The team updates the game implementation to correct the issue, including the board logic or tracking behavior, and the fix can be delivered in a new build.

setup: A tester has a completed build of Qheadache with access to gameplay, result tracking, and saved progress behavior.
action: The tester plays multiple puzzle sessions, including a full solve, an abandoned game, and a resumed saved game.
expected_observation: The tester can verify that puzzles are solvable, gameplay behaves fairly, tracking records the correct outcomes, and saved results are preserved and restored correctly.

setup: Qheadache is on the main menu with no active puzzle session running.
action: The player chooses the option to launch a new puzzle.
expected_observation: A new puzzle session starts and the puzzle board appears in a ready-to-play state.

setup: The player is in an active puzzle session with moves already made on the board.
action: The player either solves the puzzle, selects the give-up option, or closes the game.
expected_observation: The current puzzle session ends and the game transitions away from the active board to the appropriate completion, abandonment, or exit state.

setup: The player has just completed a level by reaching the solved puzzle state.
action: The game records the completed level at the end of the session.
expected_observation: The completed level progress is saved so the result remains available after the session ends.

setup: The player is in the middle of a puzzle and the game detects a safe opportunity to persist the current state without disrupting play.
action: A safe save point occurs during normal gameplay.
expected_observation: The current puzzle progress is saved during play and the board remains usable without interruption or loss of the ongoing session.

setup: The player is partway through a puzzle and has not yet solved it.
action: The player closes Qheadache in the middle of the puzzle and later opens the game again.
expected_observation: The game preserves as much of the current puzzle state as possible and allows the player to continue later from the retained progress.

setup: The player has a puzzle session in progress and the game is unexpectedly interrupted or closed suddenly.
action: The game is restarted after the interruption.
expected_observation: The last known safe puzzle state is restored instead of loading a corrupted or partially updated board.

setup: The player is in an active puzzle session with a block arrangement that makes a specific move impossible under the puzzle rules.
action: The player attempts the invalid move, such as moving a block into an occupied or blocked space.
expected_observation: The game refuses the move, shows immediate clear feedback explaining why it is not allowed, and keeps the player in the current session.

setup: The player has an active puzzle board with a known current state and saved progress already established.
action: The player performs an invalid move attempt that the rules do not permit.
expected_observation: The board state remains unchanged, no progress is lost, and the game continues from the same puzzle position after the rejected move.

setup: A puzzle is in progress and the player has already made at least one valid move.
action: The player clicks the Undo control immediately after the most recent move.
expected_observation: The last move is reversed, the board returns to the previous valid state, and the player's move count reflects the undone move without any penalty or loss of progress.

setup: A puzzle is currently active and the player has made several moves.
action: The player selects Restart from the in-game controls and confirms the restart if prompted.
expected_observation: The active puzzle resets to its initial starting layout, the move count for the current attempt returns to the start, and the player is not penalized for restarting.

setup: A puzzle is active and the board is visible without any hint currently displayed.
action: The player requests a hint using the in-game Hint control.
expected_observation: A subtle hint is shown on demand, such as a highlighted piece or suggested move, and no hint appears unless the player explicitly requests it.

setup: A board transition or move animation is already in progress after the player initiated a valid action.
action: The player rapidly clicks additional tiles or presses move inputs before the current action finishes processing.
expected_observation: Only the first input is processed; the extra inputs are ignored, no input queue is formed, and the board ends in a single predictable state corresponding to the accepted action.

setup: The player is on an active puzzle board and the interface is responsive.
action: The player performs rapid repeated clicks on the same valid move target or alternating valid inputs during a short interval.
expected_observation: The board state remains stable and predictable, with no duplicated moves, skipped states, or corrupted layout, and the final board reflects only the legitimate processed inputs.

setup: The player has an active session with an ongoing puzzle and the game has access to session tracking data.
action: The player continues playing until the puzzle is completed.
expected_observation: The system records the session details, current puzzle state, completion time, move count, and score, and these values are available for later progress or stats display.

setup: The player has completed at least one puzzle or has previously attempted a puzzle that ended without completion.
action: The player opens the Progress or Stats area and views the history section.
expected_observation: A history of completed puzzles or attempts is shown, including past results or attempt records rather than only the current active session.

setup: The player has one or more completed puzzles and an active session with recorded move and time data.
action: The player opens the simple progress view from the game interface.
expected_observation: The view shows puzzles completed, the current time on the active puzzle, moves made, and best results when available in a clear, concise layout.

setup: The game is running and the player is at the main menu or in-game interface.
action: The player opens the dedicated Progress or Stats menu area.
expected_observation: A progress/statistics screen is displayed that provides access to the player's progress information and summary statistics.

setup: The player is viewing the Progress or Stats area and export functionality is available.
action: The player selects the Export Stats option.
expected_observation: The system exports the player's stats from the same Progress or Stats area and presents the export result without leaving the statistics context.

setup: The player is in the stats export flow with no optional detail settings selected.
action: The player exports stats using the default export option.
expected_observation: The exported file contains basic stats only, such as completion and play summary information, without additional detailed session records.

setup: The Progress or Stats area includes an optional detailed export setting and the player can choose whether to include session records.
action: The player enables the option to include detailed session records and exports stats.
expected_observation: The exported stats file includes the additional session records when the feature is supported; if detailed export is not supported, the option is not offered or is clearly unavailable.

setup: The player has just completed a stats export from the Progress or Stats area.
action: The export operation finishes successfully.
expected_observation: A clear confirmation message appears stating that the export succeeded and includes the file name or file location of the exported stats.

setup: The player is in the Progress or Stats area with progress data available.
action: The player selects the overall progress view from the available statistics options.
expected_observation: The system displays a selectable overall progress view summarizing the player's progress rather than only showing a single recent session.

setup: The Progress or Stats area supports a summarized view with expandable details.
action: The player clicks the progress item or detail toggle to reveal more information.
expected_observation: Additional progress details become visible behind the extra click, while the initial view remains concise until the player expands it.

setup: The player has completed at least one puzzle session and the game has already recorded previous scores, completion times, and move counts for that profile.
action: The player opens the progress or challenge history view and replays a previously completed challenge.
expected_observation: The game shows the recorded score, time, and progress history for completed challenges, and the replayed challenge can be started again with the prior results available for comparison.

setup: The game is installed on a device that has no active internet connection and no network access is available.
action: The player launches the game, completes a puzzle, and exits the session normally.
expected_observation: The game starts and runs offline, the completed progress is saved locally on the device, and the player can reopen the game later and see the saved progress without needing internet access.

setup: The game installer is available on a clean computer with no additional runtime services, companion apps, or background game services installed.
action: The player installs the game and launches it from the installed shortcut or application entry.
expected_observation: The game installs successfully using the provided installer alone, launches without requiring extra services to be configured, and opens to the main menu or starting screen.

setup: A new player is starting the game for the first time and has no prior gameplay experience or saved progress.
action: The player begins the first tutorial or first challenge and follows the on-screen instructions and visual hints.
expected_observation: The game presents simple beginner instructions, clear visual guidance, and an easier first level or challenge that helps the player understand how to play without being overwhelmed.

setup: The player has already completed several earlier challenges and is continuing through the game in the same profile.
action: The player starts the next available challenge after several successful completions.
expected_observation: The new challenge is noticeably more difficult than earlier ones, for example by increasing puzzle complexity, reducing hints, or introducing additional constraints as the player progresses.

setup: The player has reached a more advanced stage of play where detailed performance tracking is relevant.
action: The player opens the active puzzle screen during an advanced challenge.
expected_observation: Time elapsed, move count, and score are displayed prominently and are easy to notice while playing, making performance feedback more visible for experienced players.

setup: The player is in the middle of a puzzle session and the game is closed unexpectedly or interrupted before the session ends.
action: The player relaunches the game after the abrupt exit or interruption.
expected_observation: The game offers an easy way to continue from the interrupted session, such as a resume option or automatic return to the last active puzzle state.

setup: The player is actively playing a puzzle and reaches a valid safe state that can be preserved by the game.
action: The application exits suddenly, such as from a crash, device restart, or forced close immediately after the safe state is captured.
expected_observation: After relaunch, the game restores the most recently captured safe state rather than an older state, lost progress is minimized, and the player resumes from the latest preserved point.

setup: A saved game file or saved result exists but is partially damaged, unreadable, or otherwise cannot be parsed correctly.
action: The player launches the game and the system attempts to load the corrupted save data.
expected_observation: The game detects the unreadable save data, shows a non-blocking recovery message or falls back to recovery handling, and continues running so the rest of the application remains usable.

setup: The game has detected corrupted save data during startup or when loading a previous session.
action: The player chooses the option to start a new session instead of restoring the corrupted save.
expected_observation: The game starts a fresh session successfully, does not require the damaged save to be repaired first, and allows the player to continue playing normally.

setup: No save error, recovery event, or other actual problem is occurring during normal play.
action: The player navigates menus and plays a normal challenge without triggering any failure conditions.
expected_observation: No warning, toast, popup, or other cue is shown during normal play; subtle cues appear only when a real save failure or recovery event occurs.

setup: The game is running with internet access available and update checking is enabled as an optional feature.
action: The player reaches the main menu or chooses the update check option from a settings or menu screen.
expected_observation: The game performs an update check without interrupting gameplay, and the player can continue using the application normally while the check occurs or after it completes.

setup: An important update is available and the player has just finished a puzzle or returned to a menu screen.
action: The game detects the update while the player is at a natural pause point rather than during active play.
expected_observation: An update prompt appears only at the end of a game or in a menu context, not in the middle of play, and the prompt is presented in an unobtrusive way.

setup: An update prompt is currently visible to the player after an important update has been detected.
action: The player chooses the dismiss, later, or close option on the update prompt.
expected_observation: The prompt closes immediately, the player returns to the game or menu without disruption, and gameplay can continue normally.

setup: The player has completed one or more sessions and wants to keep a local copy of their statistics.
action: The player chooses the local stats export option and selects a save location on the device.
expected_observation: The game creates a readable local export file containing the player's stats, and the file can be opened, kept, or shared outside the game without requiring a network connection.

setup: The player is on the game's main menu with update checking and stats export features available, and no account has been created or signed in.
action: The player opens the update check screen and starts a stats export from the progress or results view.
expected_observation: The system completes both actions without asking the player to register, sign in, or provide account credentials.

setup: The player has selected an export of gameplay statistics, and the export destination or service is unavailable so the export cannot complete normally.
action: The player confirms stats export.
expected_observation: A plain-language message explains that the export failed, and it clearly states whether the statistics were saved somewhere else, such as a local file or temporary location.

setup: The player has opened the game's update check option while the device is offline or the update server is unreachable.
action: The player requests an update check.
expected_observation: The system shows no disruptive error dialog, reports the connection issue in a quiet manner, and offers a simple option to try again later.

setup: The player is in an active game session or browsing the main menu while an update check or stats export is about to be attempted.
action: The update check fails to connect or the stats export fails to complete.
expected_observation: The game remains open and playable, the current session is not interrupted or closed, and the player can continue using the app normally.

setup: The player launches the game on a supported desktop platform and begins a normal play session.
action: The player navigates menus, starts a match, finishes a level, and returns to the main screen.
expected_observation: The experience remains smooth and lightweight, with no persistent pop-ups, forced sign-in prompts, or repeated interruptions that break the flow of play.

setup: The player has accumulated progress across multiple sessions and opens the progress or summary view.
action: The player selects the overall progress screen.
expected_observation: Progress is presented in a simple lightweight format, such as brief totals or a compact summary, without dense charts, cluttered dashboards, or long blocks of explanatory text.

setup: The player has completed at least one full game and can access restart or challenge options from the results or menu screen.
action: The player starts a replayable challenge from the completed-game flow.
expected_observation: The game presents a clear challenge that can be played again with meaningful objective or progression feedback, making the replay feel purposeful rather than identical and empty.

setup: The sponsor has not announced any change to platform support, and the product is being evaluated for the first version release.
action: A project stakeholder reviews the release scope for supported devices.
expected_observation: Mobile support is not included in the first-version scope and is treated as out of scope unless the sponsor explicitly approves it later.

setup: The player is using the first version of the game on a supported desktop system.
action: The player looks for automatic update behavior after launching the game.
expected_observation: The game does not silently install updates in the background, and any update-related behavior is limited to non-automatic checking unless the sponsor later changes the rule.

setup: The game is installed as the first version on a desktop device with no network connection available.
action: The player starts the game and accesses normal gameplay and progress features.
expected_observation: The game launches and remains playable without requiring a network connection, account creation, or third-party service access.

setup: The player has completed gameplay and the system is preparing to save progress or statistics.
action: The system stores the player's progress and any exportable stats.
expected_observation: Only minimal save data is retained, and no personal information is collected unless there is a clearly justified reason for it.

setup: The player has recent progress that has not yet been saved, and the next save operation must choose between preserving progress and reducing file size.
action: The game performs a save after recent play activity.
expected_observation: The system preserves the current game state and recent progress first, even if that results in a slightly larger save file.

setup: The first version of the game is installed and a player account or online protection service is not part of the product design.
action: The player starts the game and moves through normal menus and gameplay.
expected_observation: The game does not require heavy account security steps, online identity verification, or third-party protection services to play.

setup: A saved game file has been damaged or partially corrupted before the game starts.
action: The player launches the game and the system attempts to load the corrupted save.
expected_observation: The system detects the corrupted data with a basic integrity check, recovers cleanly by ignoring or replacing the bad save, and does not crash or display nonsensical progress.

setup: The system has detected a save file that appears tampered with, and the response would not affect honest players negatively.
action: The player opens the affected save file or starts the game with that save present.
expected_observation: The system marks the save as unreliable in a limited, non-disruptive way only when that can be done safely, while avoiding unnecessary penalties or problems for legitimate players.

setup: A player has a local save that the game can open, but one section appears inconsistent after recovery, while the rest of the save contains valid recent progress.
action: The player starts the game and opens that save file.
expected_observation: The game keeps the valid progress, resets only the affected stats or corrupted section, and shows a plain-language message explaining what was fixed or reset.

setup: The player has completed several recent puzzles and the latest session data is still within the normal recent-history window.
action: The game performs its automatic storage management during or after saving.
expected_observation: The player's recent puzzle results, current streak, and other meaningful recent progress remain unchanged in the save.

setup: The player has a long puzzle history with older completed sessions that are no longer needed in full detail, along with recorded totals and best results.
action: The game performs save maintenance that reduces storage usage.
expected_observation: Older detailed records are replaced with a summary, while overall totals, completion counts, and best results remain intact.

setup: The player's save storage is getting close to its limit but is still usable.
action: The player continues playing and creates new progress that triggers save monitoring.
expected_observation: A warning appears before the save reaches a critical problem, giving the player advance notice that storage is getting tight.

setup: The save contains both very old detailed puzzle history and newer recent progress from the current play session.
action: The game needs to reduce save size to free storage space.
expected_observation: The oldest detailed history is trimmed or summarized first, while recent progress and current-session data are preserved in full.

setup: The player's save file has reached the storage limit, but the game can still preserve essential state by reducing older detail.
action: The player finishes a puzzle and the game attempts to save the new result.
expected_observation: The game completes the save as safely as possible, preserves essential progress, and informs the player that older detailed records were condensed.

setup: A local save contains signs of obvious tampering, and checking it would not interfere with normal play or corrupt valid data.
action: The player opens the save file in the game.
expected_observation: The game detects the tampering, flags the save as suspicious, and responds without disrupting honest player progress in unaffected saves.

setup: The player is in the middle of a move, animation, or puzzle transition that is already being processed.
action: The player taps or clicks the same action button repeatedly in rapid succession.
expected_observation: Only the first valid input is accepted; extra rapid inputs are ignored until the current action finishes.

setup: A save failure or recovery event occurs during normal gameplay.
action: The game handles the failure or recovery and returns control to the player.
expected_observation: The player receives a small non-blocking cue, such as a brief banner or toast, and can continue playing without being forced into a full-screen interruption.

setup: The player is playing normally and the game has either just saved successfully or is between puzzles, with no immediate decision required.
action: The game needs to notify the player about save-related status or storage reduction.
expected_observation: The game uses a subtle notification during normal play; if the player must approve or acknowledge condensed data, a modal dialog is shown instead.

setup: A save status problem has already been shown to the player and the underlying problem remains unresolved.
action: The player continues navigating menus or returns to the puzzle screen without fixing the issue.
expected_observation: The game does not repeat the same warning unnecessarily; it only reminds the player again if the problem is still present and relevant.

setup: The game is installed on the player's device with local storage available and no cloud sync requirement enabled.
action: The player completes a puzzle and exits to trigger saving.
expected_observation: The player's progress is written to local storage on the device and is available again when the game is reopened on that same device.

setup: The player has selected the export stats option and the export feature is available in the current build.
action: The player exports puzzle statistics to a local file.
expected_observation: The system creates a readable local stats file that can be opened and inspected by a person or standard file viewer without special tooling.

setup: Update checks are enabled in the game's settings and network access is available.
action: The player opens the game or selects the update-check option.
expected_observation: The game sends an update-check communication and shows the result of that check to the player; when update checks are disabled, no such communication occurs.

setup: A new player launches the game for the first time on a typical device with no prior configuration.
action: The player starts a puzzle without reading a manual or completing a setup wizard.
expected_observation: The main controls, puzzle state, and basic navigation are immediately understandable, with minimal or no setup required before play begins.

setup: A player completes a puzzle round in Qheadache and returns to the results screen.
action: The player finishes the challenge with a recorded time and move count.
expected_observation: The results screen clearly shows the player's performance using understandable metrics such as completion time, moves used, and success status.

setup: The Qheadache game package is prepared for distribution on a typical consumer device.
action: A player downloads, installs, and launches the game from the distributed package.
expected_observation: The game installs and starts without requiring heavy dependencies or a large setup process, and the distributed package remains easy to share and store.

setup: A player has completed at least one puzzle challenge and has access to the main menu.
action: The player finishes a round and is offered the option to replay or start a new challenge.
expected_observation: The game presents an engaging completion experience with a clear replay option and a satisfying prompt that encourages the player to try another challenge.

setup: A player is actively playing a puzzle and the game is configured to save results at the end of the round.
action: The player completes the puzzle and the system writes the result to storage while transitioning back to the menu.
expected_observation: The result is saved successfully, the gameplay flow continues without freezing or crashing, and the player returns to a usable game state.

setup: A young beginner opens the game for the first time on a small screen device.
action: The player views the main menu and starts a puzzle.
expected_observation: The interface uses simple labels, large readable controls, and an uncluttered layout so the child can identify the main actions without confusion.

setup: The game contains an active puzzle board, timing is running, and player progress information is stored between sessions.
action: The player makes several moves, pauses the game, and then resumes from the saved state.
expected_observation: Board moves, timer updates, and stored player progress all remain consistent before and after pause/resume, with no broken interactions or incorrect state changes.

setup: The application contains a large collection of stored puzzle records and recent results.
action: The player opens the high scores, past results, or puzzle history screen from the main menu.
expected_observation: The screen opens promptly, remains responsive while browsing the records, and the application does not become noticeably slow or memory-heavy.

setup: A puzzle board is displayed and a player has selected a single movable piece.
action: The player rapidly clicks or taps the same piece twice during one move attempt.
expected_observation: Only one move is registered, the board state remains predictable, and the piece does not jump, duplicate, or apply the action twice.

setup: A player is actively solving a puzzle and has made an incorrect move.
action: The player makes a mistake and then attempts to continue solving the challenge.
expected_observation: The game preserves the challenge by not auto-solving or removing difficulty, while still giving the player a fair way to recover, continue, or try again without unnecessary frustration.

setup: The Qheadache game is installed and running on a standard device with normal user interaction.
action: The player navigates through the menu, starts a puzzle, and completes a round.
expected_observation: The application remains straightforward to use and behaves reliably throughout the session, without introducing complicated steps, unstable behavior, or confusing interactions.

setup: The system has saved multiple puzzle records and determines that compression or indexing may reduce storage size without affecting reliability.
action: The application saves a new result using the storage approach selected for that data set.
expected_observation: The saved data remains compact while the record can still be read back correctly later, and no corruption or loss of result information is introduced.

setup: The game library contains multiple puzzle packs, but the player needs only one specific puzzle set to begin a session.
action: The player selects a single puzzle mode or level from the menu.
expected_observation: Only the needed puzzle data is loaded for the chosen mode, the rest of the library is not loaded into view unnecessarily, and the game starts without a full-library delay.

setup: The player is in the middle of solving a puzzle and optional non-gameplay features are available, such as reminders or feature prompts.
action: A prompt for a non-essential feature becomes available while the puzzle is active.
expected_observation: The prompt appears subtly and does not block gameplay, obscure the board, or demand immediate attention away from the puzzle.

setup: The game is loading saved sessions and one save file on disk contains corrupted data.
action: The player opens the saved game list or resumes a session that includes the corrupted file.
expected_observation: The corrupted save is skipped or quarantined, the player is not blocked from entering the game, and the remaining valid saves continue to work normally.

setup: The application contains saved results, and one result entry cannot be decoded or read correctly.
action: The player opens the results history or score summary screen that includes the unreadable entry.
expected_observation: The unreadable result is handled without stopping the application, the rest of the results remain accessible, and the player can continue using the game normally.

setup: The player has an active game in progress with unsaved movement since the last confirmed checkpoint, and the game is running normally on the current device.
action: The game is abruptly closed or the device loses power during play, then the player relaunches the game.
expected_observation: On restart, the game restores the most recent safe saved state rather than a partially completed move sequence, and the player can continue from the last confirmed position without corruption or missing progress.

setup: The game is open on the main menu or in an active session, and the network connection to the update service is unavailable.
action: The system attempts to check for updates while the player keeps the game open.
expected_observation: The update check fails without interrupting gameplay, no blocking error dialog appears, and the player remains able to start or continue playing normally.

setup: The player has completed a game session and chooses to export statistics, while the export destination is unavailable or rejects the write request.
action: The player initiates the stats export action.
expected_observation: The game shows a clear message that the statistics export could not be completed, and the application remains responsive so the player can continue using the game normally.

setup: The player is in the middle of an active game and the storage location for saving progress is nearly full or cannot accept additional save data.
action: The game attempts to save progress after a move, checkpoint, or session change.
expected_observation: The game warns the player that storage is limited, preserves the essential progress that can still be saved, and does not discard the entire game state or crash.

setup: The player has an existing saved session, then switches to another session or leaves the game unopened for an extended period before returning.
action: The player reopens the game and selects the prior session to continue.
expected_observation: The game loads cleanly into the correct session without losing the player's place, and the board or state resumes from the last known location instead of resetting or opening the wrong session.

setup: The game is being evaluated for supported platforms, with no mobile-specific version or controls currently committed.
action: A player attempts to access the game on a mobile device.
expected_observation: The system does not claim mobile support as a released feature; if mobile access is unavailable, the game presents a clear unsupported-platform outcome rather than an inconsistent or partially working mobile experience.

setup: The first version of the game is installed on a player device, and automatic updates are not enabled as a defined release feature.
action: The player launches the game and waits for the system to look for updates without manually requesting it.
expected_observation: The game remains playable without relying on automatic update behavior, and no mandatory update flow interrupts access unless a future sponsor decision explicitly adds that capability.

setup: The game is configured with standard save behavior, and no adaptive autosave timing policy has been finalized.
action: The player performs normal gameplay for an extended period, including short and long pauses between moves.
expected_observation: The game continues using its defined save behavior without exposing a contradictory adaptive-autosave promise, and progress remains protected according to the currently available save mechanism.

setup: The game stores progress data on a device where available storage is being consumed by other files, and no final storage threshold has been specified.
action: The player continues playing until a save operation is attempted under constrained storage conditions.
expected_observation: When storage pressure occurs, the game behaves defensively by warning the player and preserving progress as much as possible, without relying on any undocumented fixed capacity limit.

setup: The player has completed gameplay and opens the statistics export feature, while the product has not yet decided whether to include detailed session records.
action: The player requests a stats export and examines the exported content.
expected_observation: The export contains only the currently defined statistics fields and does not present detailed session records as a guaranteed part of the output unless that capability is later approved.
